descriptors.concept_name: Reference Date for Further Public Offer
descriptors.definition: An issuer must fulfill all regulatory conditions for a further public offer on both the date of filing the draft offer document with the Board and the final offer document with the Registrar of Companies. This dual-filing timeline ensures continuous compliance before securities can be issued to the public.
inclusion: Filing date with the Board
Filing date with the Registrar of Companies
exclusion: Allotment date
Listing date
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from post-issue listing approvals and general conditions which operate on separate regulatory timelines.

descriptors.concept_name: Entities not eligible to make a further public offer (Regulation 102)
descriptors.definition: Certain issuers are disqualified from undertaking a further public offer if the issuer, its promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders are debarred from capital markets. Disqualifications also extend to wilful defaulters, fraudulent borrowers, and fugitive economic offenders.
inclusion: Entities with past debarment periods already expired at filing
Issuers with directors linked to debarred companies
exclusion: Issuers with expired debarment periods
Entities compliant with all capital market regulations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general operational conditions by focusing entirely on personal or corporate integrity and regulatory penalty histories.

descriptors.concept_name: Eligibility requirements for further public offer (Regulation 103)
descriptors.definition: An issuer must not have changed its name within the preceding one year unless at least half of its revenue comes from the activity reflecting the new name. Failure to meet this revenue threshold requires using the book building process, allocating seventy-five percent of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers, and offering full subscription refunds upon failure.
inclusion: Issuers with unchanged names for one year
Name-changed issuers earning fifty percent revenue from the new activity
exclusion: Issuers failing revenue thresholds without opting for book building and QIB allotment safeguards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from entity disqualifications by imposing specific financial and procedural hurdles related to corporate identity shifts.

descriptors.definition: An issuer executing a further public offer must secure in-principle stock exchange listings, utilize depositories for dematerialization, fully pay or forfeit partly paid shares, and arrange verifiable finance for seventy-five percent of specific capital expenditure projects. Additionally, limits are imposed on amounts raised for general corporate purposes and unidentified acquisitions or investments.
inclusion: Application to stock exchanges
Depository agreements
Project financing arrangements
exclusion: Active partly paid-up equity shares without forfeiture
Unverified financing arrangements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from eligibility rules by dictating structural prerequisites and fund utilization caps rather than historical track records.

descriptors.concept_name: Additional conditions for an offer for sale (Regulation 105)
descriptors.definition: Shares offered for sale to the public must be fully paid-up and held by the selling shareholder for a minimum of one year prior to filing the draft offer document. Specific exemptions apply to infrastructure-focused government entities, tribunal-approved business restructuring schemes, and bonus issues derived from existing free reserves.
instrument_references: Sections 230 to 234 of the Companies Act, 2013
inclusion: Fully paid shares held for at least one year
Shares derived from conversion of convertible securities meeting combined holding periods
exclusion: Shares held for less than one year without statutory exemption
Partly paid-up equity shares
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from primary issuances by enforcing retrospective holding duration constraints directly onto existing shareholders.

descriptors.concept_name: Eligibility of issuer to make FPO of convertible debt instruments
descriptors.definition: An issuer may execute a further public offer of convertible debt instruments only if its equity shares are already listed on a recognized stock exchange. Furthermore, the issuer must not remain in default of interest or principal repayments on public debt instruments for more than six months.
inclusion: Issuers with listed equity shares
Issuers compliant with debt repayment schedules
exclusion: Issuers with unlisted equity shares
Issuers defaulting on public debt payments exceeding six months
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity FPOs by mandating prior equity listing status and specific debt-servicing track records.

descriptors.concept_name: Eligibility of issuer to make FPO of convertible debt instruments
descriptors.definition: An issuer may execute a further public offer of convertible debt instruments only if its equity shares are already listed on a recognized stock exchange. Furthermore, the issuer must not remain in default of interest or principal repayments on public debt instruments for more than six months.
inclusion: Issuers with listed equity shares
Issuers compliant with debt repayment schedules
exclusion: Issuers with unlisted equity shares
Issuers defaulting on public debt payments exceeding six months
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity FPOs by mandating prior equity listing status and specific debt-servicing track records.

descriptors.concept_name: Additional requirements for issue of convertible debt instruments (Regulation 107)
descriptors.definition: Issuers offering public convertible debt instruments must secure credit ratings, appoint debenture trustees, and establish debenture redemption reserves under statutory guidelines. Secured instruments require unencumbered asset cover sufficient to cover principal amounts, with prior institutional consents obtained for second or pari passu charges.
instrument_references: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993
inclusion: Credit ratings from rating agencies
Debenture trust appointments
Asset security coverage for secured debt
exclusion: Unsecured debt lacking required asset covers or trustee structures
Debt issues without mandatory redemption reserves
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from basic FPO rules by introducing rigorous credit safety, trust administration, and asset encumbrance mandates.

descriptors.concept_name: Roll over of non-convertible portion of partly convertible debt instruments (Regulation 108)
descriptors.definition: The non-convertible portion of large partly convertible debt instruments exceeding ten crore rupees can be rolled over if approved by seventy-five percent of holders by value via postal ballot. The issuer must provide audited cash flow statements, redeem holdings of dissenting investors, and secure fresh credit ratings before maturity.
inclusion: Postal ballot approval by seventy-five percent value holders
Redemption provisions for dissenting debt holders
exclusion: Roll-overs executed without required value-holder consent
Omission of mandatory auditor liquidity reports
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard debt redemption by providing restructuring mechanisms through institutional voting thresholds.

descriptors.concept_name: Conversion of optionally convertible debt instruments into equity share capital (Regulation 109)
descriptors.definition: Optionally convertible debt instruments cannot convert to equity without explicit positive consent from holders, treating silence as non-consent. For listed instruments exceeding ten crore rupees without upfront pricing, holders must be granted an exit option unless a price formula or upper limit was disclosed initially.
inclusion: Explicit positive consent collection
Redemption provisions for unconverted instruments
exclusion: Automatic conversion based on non-response to notices
Conversion without pre-disclosed pricing formulas or holder options
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from mandatory conversions by protecting investor optionality and requiring affirmative confirmation.

descriptors.concept_name: Issue of convertible debt instruments for financing (Regulation 110) An issuer shall not issue convertible debt instruments for financing or for providing loans to or for acquiring shares of any person who is part of the promoter group or group companies:
descriptors.definition: Issuing convertible debt instruments to finance, lend to, or acquire shares of promoter group entities or group companies is prohibited. An exception applies permitting fully convertible debt instruments for these purposes if conversion occurs in less than eighteen months.
inclusion: Fully convertible debt instruments converting under eighteen months for group financing
exclusion: Partly or non-convertible debt instruments utilized for promoter group loans or share acquisitions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general corporate financing rules by placing strict guardrails on intra-group fund routing via convertible instruments.

descriptors.definition: Issuers may attach warrants to specified securities in further public offers provided their tenure does not exceed eighteen months. Upfront collection of at least twenty-five percent of the exercise price or cap price formula is mandatory, and unexercised warrant considerations must be forfeited after three months.
inclusion: Warrants with a maximum eighteen-month tenure
Upfront collection of twenty-five percent consideration
Forfeiture of unexercised warrant deposits
exclusion: Warrants exceeding eighteen-month tenures
Issues lacking upfront consideration payments
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from debt instruments by providing optional equity acquisition rights tied to upfront pricing parameters.
